title: Whether the object of faith can be false
pass_a_gloss: Article XIV. Whether the object of faith can be false. 1. Some assert that faith's object can be false — if God (per impossibile) revealed something false, or if someone believes what is in fact false, thinking it revealed by God. 2. We answer: the object of divine faith, formally considered, cannot be false; because divine faith rests on God's testimony, who is truth itself and can neither deceive nor be deceived. If something false is believed, it is not divine faith, but error or fallacious human faith. 3. What some say about faith concerning conditional propositions or future contingents does not make faith's object false: for God reveals true things, even about contingents, according to his decree.
pass_b_english: Article XIV. Whether the object of faith can be false.
1. Some say faith's object can be false — if God (per impossibile) revealed a falsehood, or if someone believes what is in fact false, taking it as revealed.

2. Formally, divine faith's object cannot be false. It rests on God's testimony; he is truth itself and can neither deceive nor be deceived. Believing a falsehood is error or fallacious human faith, not divine faith.
3. Faith about conditionals or future contingents does not make the object false: God reveals what is true, even about contingents, according to his decree.
source_text:
ART. XIV.
An objectum fidei possit esse falsum.

1. Non desunt qui asserant objectum fidei posse esse falsum — si DEUS (per impossibile) falsum revelaret, vel si aliquis credat id quod de facto falsum est, putans a DEO revelatum.

2. Respondemus: Objectum fidei divinae, formaliter spectatum, non potest esse falsum; quia fides divina nititur DEI testimonio, qui est ipsa veritas & nec fallere nec falli potest. Si quid falsum creditur, non est fides divina, sed error vel fides humana fallax.

3. Quod aliqui dicunt de fide quae versatur circa propositiones conditionales vel de futuris contingentibus, non facit objectum fidei esse falsum: DEUS enim vera revelat, etiam de contingentibus, secundum decretum suum.
